accuracy.evidence: Matches Development Matters (2021) Reception PSED (respectful relationships, considering others' feelings), the ELGs Building Relationships and Managing Self, and the NSPCC PANTS message that your body belongs to you and you can say no. 'About an arm away' is given as a comfortable distance for most people, not a rule; family hugs are framed as 'if we both want', and a no from anyone (including Grandad) is respected. Every sort answer and line position was checked: START spacing 0.1 of width squashes all four bubbles (radius 0.1), Show me positions 0.12/0.37/0.63/0.88 give 0.25+ gaps so none overlap.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets real early-years slips named in the adult text: best friends never need space (line predict, m1, challenge 'close'), only words count so stepping back or turning away is missed (signs predict, p3, m6, challenge 'sign'), hug first then ask (p4, challenge 'push'), asking again after a no (ask scene 'nag', m2, challenge 'nag'), and the child must accept any hug (m7, m9, challenge 'mine'), plus hugging a child you do not know (size scene, m5, challenge 'size').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbubble is about distance and consent: a line of four children whose drawn bubbles turn red when they overlap and green when dragged an arm apart, a body-language spotting grid with three non-verbal space signs and three invitations, a hug-request dialogue where yes, no and 'high five instead' each need a different action, and a hug-or-wave sort for family against people you do not know. It is not the manners lab (flagplease) or a feelings lab; the lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the idea by acting: dragging a child shows the bubbles change colour live and the aria-label reports how many are squashed; a wrong hug response gets 'Cat did not say yes to a hug'; tapping a smile as a space sign explains it is an invitation. The step summaries only confirm what the child just did (an arm apart, no means okay, family vs people you do not know).

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Yes, friends do not mind' standing close to Bea (her bubble turns red), 'No, they did not say stop' for a friend who steps back (the signs grid counts stepping back as a space sign), and 'Hug anyway, we are friends' after a no (the ask scene rejects it and names why).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; wrong options carry seven tagged messages: close (stand an arm away), sign (stepping back means space), push (ask first, hug only on yes), nag (no means no), mine (your bubble is yours, say please give me space), grab (use words and tell a grown-up), size (keep a big bubble with people you do not know). Answer order rotates each question.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and words a 4 to 5 year old uses every day (bubble, arm, hug, step back, okay); lab prompts give one instruction each and every card has a picture plus at most five words. Curriculum terms (PSED, consent, body language) appear only in the adult text, within the validator's readability limits.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: what the bubble is; too close vs just right; signs a friend wants space; ask before a hug and your own bubble. Adult paragraphs: curriculum placement, how to practise at home, common mistakes, what the lab does. No stock phrases; the content gate's filler and duplicate checks pass.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px the canvas uses the tall phone ratio; sort tiles are a 3-column grid about 115 px wide, the line scene's kids have a hit radius of at least 24 px and every child has left and right arrow buttons below, and answer pills are at least 48 px tall. The iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me with nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin (each card to Too close or Just right, move each child left or right, each space sign, each hug answer, each person to hug or wave). The canvas aria-label reports each result and the squashed-bubble count while dragging; red/green bubbles also differ by solid vs dashed outline, so colour is not the only cue. axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs clean in light and dark themes.
